phenolics are highly variable in larch heartwood at all levels of investigation (taxa, genotypes, individuals, trees, wood parts, years); the variability is related to the genetic background and environmental conditions; phenolics are the major determinants of wood colour; the phenolic content of hybrid larches is intermediate to the two parent taxa, European larch and Japanese larch; and the phenolic composition is different in European larch and in Japanese larch, but similar in
phenolic contents are highly variable at different hierarchical levels (taxa, genotypes and trees) and that phenolics are linked to colour parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic improvement of larch heart wood quality in terms of colour and phenolics.
the distribution of heartwood extractive content in hybrid larch trees and in their related parents.
the genetic control of heartwood extractive variability in hybrid larch and its parents, and its link with wood colour parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phenolics are not the only factors that influence wood colour and vice versa.
Taxifolin and DHK contents are not good indicators of wood colour parameters.
the phenolic content of larch heartwoods is highly variable, but that the phenolic profile and colour parameters are strongly related.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

phenolic content in hybrid larch heartwood is intermediate between European and Japanese larchs and that it is positively correlated with red–green colour intensity and negatively correlated with lightness.
the colour and extractive content of hybrid larches is in between the two parent taxa, European and Japanese larchs, with the exception of DHK, which was higher in hybrid larch.
phenolic compounds are not the only compounds responsible for wood colour in larch, but they are certainly a major contributor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interspecific hybrid larch has a higher phenolic content than its parents and that it is a good candidate for further breeding.
phenolics are a major determinant of wood quality in larches.
phenolic content and composition are highly heritable and can be used as selection criteria for breeding programmes.
